decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks (title, URL, description, tags)”; round 1 client: “This does what I need for saving ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation records URL-based bookmark creation, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit ... bookmarks (title, URL, description, tags)”; round 1 client: “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: The presented add and edit stages allow title and description changes before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents the editable fields as “title, URL, description, tags,” omitting a note field or rendered markdown note; round 1 client gives only general approval: “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented bookmark editor lacks the reference-required note capability. The client does not identify or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks”; round 1 client: “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: The recorded delete behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tags — comma-separated, deduplicated”; round 1 client approves the application generally.
decisions.note: Comma-separated tags permit one or more tags to be assigned, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker describes tag entry only as “comma-separated, deduplicated”; round 1 client says only “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: The presentation does not establish whether existing-tag autocomplete is present or absent, and the client does not clarify it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “click a tag (in the sidebar or on a card) to filter”; round 1 client says the app meets their organizing and finding needs.
decisions.note: Selecting a specific tag to filter bookmarks conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Live search across title, URL, description, and tags,” omitting note content from the stated search fields; round 1 client gives general approval without discussing search-field coverage.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the enumerated full-text search scope excludes the reference-required note field. The client does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “link-title auto-fetch” as something that could be added, while the current feature list only says “Favicons auto-loaded per site”; round 1 client responds, “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Offering title auto-fetch as a future addition establishes that the current save flow lacks at least one mandatory part of automatic page-metadata collection. The client's bare approval does not explicitly identify or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker asks whether to add “import/export,” presenting import as outside the current implementation; round 1 client says, “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Netscape HTML import is absent from the presented implementation. The client neither requests it nor explicitly states and accepts the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker asks whether to add “import/export,” presenting export as outside the current implementation; round 1 client says, “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export is absent from the presented implementation. The client neither requests it nor explicitly states and accepts the difference.
